Blackjack Rules

Get closer to 21 than the bank, but not over 21. Two variants, one game - played with chips, which are only points.

The rules

Two variants
17 and 4 is played with 32 cards (7 to Ace), Blackjack with 52 cards (2 to Ace). Choose the variant under New game.
Card values in 17 and 4
Ace 11, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2, the number cards 7 to 10 their value. Two aces as your first two cards are called "fire" and are the best hand.
Card values in Blackjack
Ace 1 or 11 (whichever is better for you), King, Queen and Jack 10, the number cards their value. Ace and a 10-card as your first two cards are a blackjack.
A round
Choose your bet: 5, 10 or 20 chips. You get two cards, the bank one card face up and one face down. Take more cards with "Card", or stop with "Stand". If you go over 21, you have lost at once.
The bank
When you stand, the bank turns over its card. It always follows the same rule: it draws while it has 16 or less and stands from 17. If it goes over 21, you win.
Who wins
Whoever is closer to 21 wins. You win as many chips as you bet; a blackjack wins one and a half times the bet (rounded down). Equal points: in 17 and 4 the bank wins, in Blackjack you keep your chips. A 21 with two cards (blackjack) or fire ends the round at once.
Doubling (Blackjack only)
With your first two cards you may double: your bet doubles, you get exactly one more card, and then the bank plays. You need enough chips for it. There is no splitting and no insurance.
Chips
You start with 100 chips. They are only points in the game and cannot be exchanged for anything. If you have none left, start again with 100.

Same cards, different points

Ace and King: in Blackjack they make 21 - a blackjack. In 17 and 4 they make only 15 (Ace 11, King 4).
